sections.html:
Roy is a Weber County bedroom community lying west of Interstate 15 in the Ogden-Clearfield metro area. Few businesses are based here and most residents commute. Elevation is about 4,377 feet. Hooper lies to the west, West Haven to the north, Riverdale and Ogden to the east, and Clinton and Sunset in Davis County to the south.

Roy is not one uniform market. The eastern bench holds mostly 1950s and 1960s houses, and newer building shifted west and south after about 2005. A mile can separate a 1950s starter home from a recent build with a bigger lot and fewer repairs.

sections.h2: Why Roy has so many mid-century homes
sections.html:
The town incorporated on March 10, 1937, and World War II changed it. Population jumped from 868 in 1940 to 3,723 in 1950 as Roy housed workers from nearby installations, including Hill Air Force Base, the Navy Supply Depot (now the Freeport Center) and the Defense Supply Depot. Entry-level homes then filled much of the eastern bench through the 1950s and 1960s, and building continued at the western base of the hill from the 1980s.

So many Roy sellers hold mid-century starter homes with original plumbing, older electrical panels, single-pane windows or an unfinished basement. Lenders and their buyers often want those items repaired. We take the house as it is.

Nothing shapes demand for Roy housing more than the base. I-15 exit 338 leads to its north entrance, so Roy sits right by the gate. A 2019 economic impact report put the base's annual impact at $3.7 billion, with 27,650 people counted, including 5,705 military and 16,653 civilians.

The upshot is a very large employer a short drive away. A seller working there may have to move on a set schedule after a reassignment or PCS order, and a guaranteed closing day can be worth more to them than a slightly higher price.

I-15 exit 338 connects to Utah State Route 97 (5600 South), one of the city's main roads. A FrontRunner station has served Roy since April 26, 2008, when the northern segment of the line opened.

Two sets of tracks cross the city at 2700 West, used by FrontRunner and the Union Pacific Railroad. Train noise is a real consideration for homes near that corridor, and a buyer or inspector may mention it.

  • Exit 338 leads to 5600 South and to the Hill AFB north gate.
  • FrontRunner stops at the Roy station for trips along the Wasatch Front.
  • Freight and passenger tracks both run near 2700 West.

January's mean daily high is 37 degrees Fahrenheit, July's is 94, and the record low is minus 26. Roy gets about 18.4 inches of precipitation a year, mostly in April or May.

Repeated freezing and thawing cracks concrete, strains exposed pipes and wears out asphalt shingles early. An aging roof is among the usual reasons a traditional buyer asks for a lower price.

Weber School District covers Roy entirely. Seven elementary schools, three junior highs and two high schools serve the city. Newer ones such as Haven Bay Elementary, Mountain View Junior High and West Field High may be missing from older lists, so ask the district which school an address feeds.

The Roy City Recreation Complex on the high school campus has a pool, basketball courts, a weight room, racquetball courts and an indoor track, and the Roy Aquatic Center is an outdoor complex. Each August, Roy Days brings a parade, a car show and fireworks to Roy West Park.

sections.h2: Permits for repairs before you sell
sections.html:
A permit is required for many Roy repairs and additions, filed online through the My City Inspector portal. A plan set for a one or two family dwelling must include a site plan, footing and foundation plan, floor plans, elevations, insulation R-values and energy compliance documents. State law aims for initial plan review within 14 business days of acceptance. Phone the Building Official about fees and exempt projects first.

Roy sales often stall on unpermitted work, since a lender or inspector may ask about a finished basement or converted garage. Selling as-is spares you from permitting and finishing jobs you would rather not fund.

Weber County sends Roy's tax bills, payable by November 30 unless that day lands on a weekend or holiday. Value is set as of January 1, and a primary residence gets a 45 percent exemption on the buildings and up to one acre of land.

Valuation notices typically arrive around the end of July or start of August. Appeal by September 15, or within 45 days of the notice if that is later. The county accepts late appeals only for severe circumstances: a death in the family, a dire medical emergency or a factual error in the property description.

• A bill unpaid on December 1 is delinquent.
  • Clear it in full by January 31 and the penalty is the greater of $10 or 1 percent.
  • Later, the penalty becomes the greater of $10 or 2.5 percent, with interest counted from January 1.
  • After five years of delinquency a property can go to tax sale.

Selling with taxes owed is workable, because the title company can pay the balance from your proceeds. Also ask how this year's tax will be divided between you and the buyer.

Recording a deed with the Weber County Recorder costs $45.00 for page one under HB 38 and nothing for further standard pages. A page bigger than 8.5 by 14 inches adds $2.00, and so does each description beyond 10.

sections.h2: Your options for selling a Roy house
sections.html:
Roy owners typically weigh three routes: list with an agent, sell it yourself, or sell for cash. The timeline and up-front cost differ for each.

  • Listing reaches more buyers, though it brings showings, post-inspection repair requests and the chance a loan falls through.
  • Selling it yourself saves the commission and hands marketing, contracts and disclosures to you.
  • A cash sale can close on your date with the house taken as is, a fit for inherited, tenant-occupied or neglected homes.

After decades of ownership, a Roy house may carry deferred maintenance. Request a cash offer and set it beside what you would net after repairs, carrying costs and a longer wait. Nothing obliges you to accept.

faqs.q: Is Roy, Utah in Weber County?
faqs.a: Yes, and Weber County mails the property tax bills.

faqs.q: When are Roy property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 30, unless it lands on a weekend or holiday. After that the bill is delinquent from December 1, carrying a penalty of the greater of $10 or 1 percent if cleared by January 31.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a property valuation in Roy?
faqs.a: Whichever is later of September 15 and 45 days after the valuation notice. Appeals go to the Weber County Board of Equalization, and late ones are limited to severe circumstances.

faqs.q: Does a Roy house need repairs before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No. A cash buyer can purchase a Roy house in its current condition. It still helps to tell the buyer about known problems such as roof leaks, an old furnace or unpermitted work.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited house in Roy?
faqs.a: Yes, once you have the legal authority to sell, for example as the personal representative or as an owner on the title. Talk with a Utah attorney or title company about the paperwork, then ask for a cash offer if you want a quick closing.
